title: The Twin Snowmen of Late February
skyStory: The moon slips into Scorpio, seventy-five percent lit and mysterious, wearing a dark cloak and an expression that says it knows something you do not. Scorpio loves secrets and strange connections. Tonight it has quietly arranged for two snowmen, built by two different strangers in two different towns, to wear exactly the same unusual hat. The moon winks once.

reading: On your way somewhere today you will pass a snowman wearing a striped toque, one pinecone eye and one bottle-cap eye, holding a wooden spoon up to its face like a microphone. You will laugh out loud. You will take a photo because it is too good not to.

That evening, Nancy will send you a photo of a snowman in her town: striped toque, pinecone eye, bottle-cap eye, wooden spoon microphone. DES. Two snowmen, built by two strangers, miles apart. The [[Wheel of Fortune]] is clearly in a playful mood. Accept that the universe has a sense of humour.
joel.mission: Photograph a snowman, a frost pattern, or an icicle that looks like it has a personality.
joel.omen: A snowman with mismatched eyes. Somewhere, a second snowman is wearing the exact same grin.
joel.stoneWhy: the stone Nancy wears, for matching snowmen

reading: Scorpio moons sharpen your intuition to a point, and today you will feel a strange little pull to take the long way home. Follow it. Halfway along you will meet a snowman in a striped toque with mismatched eyes and a wooden spoon raised mid-song, looking at you like an old friend.

Then your phone buzzes, and there is the same snowman in Joel's photo, miles away. Same toque, same eyes, same spoon held up for the big finale. Don't even scream. The Wood Rat knew something was coming. Your Life Path 11 has been humming all week, and now you know why.
nancy.mission: Take a slightly different route somewhere today and look closely at everything you pass.
nancy.omen: A wooden spoon somewhere it does not belong, like a windowsill or a mailbox. A coincidence is about to come and find you.
nancy.stoneWhy: the stone Joel wears, for matching snowmen

together.text: The twin snowmen have spoken. ΔΕΣ, without question. Give them names together, matching ones, and decide what they would say to each other if they ever met. Write their imaginary conversation in exactly six lines, three each, by bedtime.
